title: NIH Chest X-Ray: Stratified Train/Val/Test Splits
subtitle: Patient-level splits with class weights for 112K chest X-rays
description:
## What Makes This Different?

**The base NIH Chest X-Ray dataset gives you 112K raw images.** This companion dataset gives you **production-ready splits** so you can start training immediately.

### The Problem with the Base Dataset

When using the original NIH dataset, you must:
- ❌ Manually split 112K images into train/val/test
- ❌ Ensure no patient appears in multiple splits (data leakage)
- ❌ Balance disease distributions across splits
- ❌ Calculate class weights for the severe imbalance (Hernia: 0.4% vs No Finding: 53.8%)
- ❌ Create your own preprocessing pipeline

### What This Dataset Provides

✅ **Pre-made splits** (70/15/15) saving hours of work
✅ **Patient-level stratification** preventing data leakage
✅ **Disease-balanced splits** maintaining distributions
✅ **Computed class weights** ready for loss functions
✅ **Preprocessing config** for reproducible pipelines
✅ **CSV format** compatible with Keras, PyTorch, TensorFlow

## Quick Start

```python
import pandas as pd

# Load ready-to-use splits
train_df = pd.read_csv('/kaggle/input/nih-chest-xray-splits/train_split.csv')
val_df = pd.read_csv('/kaggle/input/nih-chest-xray-splits/val_split.csv')
test_df = pd.read_csv('/kaggle/input/nih-chest-xray-splits/test_split.csv')

# Link to base NIH images
train_df['path'] = train_df['Image Index'].apply(
    lambda x: f'/kaggle/input/nih-chest-xrays/images/{x}'
)

# Start training immediately!
```

## Dataset Composition

| Split | Images | Purpose |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Train | 78,831 (70%) | Model training |
| Val | 16,383 (15%) | Hyperparameter tuning |
| Test | 16,890 (15%) | Final evaluation |

**Total:** 112,104 images across 30,805 patients

## Files

- `train_split.csv`, `val_split.csv`, `test_split.csv` - Multi-label annotations for 14 diseases
- `preprocessing_config.json` - Disease classes, split ratios, normalization params
- `class_weights.json` - Per-disease weights (Hernia: 258x, Infiltration: 0.55x, etc.)
- `README.md` - TensorFlow/PyTorch examples, methodology, citations

## Disease Classes (14)

Atelectasis, Cardiomegaly, Consolidation, Edema, Effusion, Emphysema, Fibrosis, Hernia, Infiltration, Mass, Nodule, Pleural_Thickening, Pneumonia, Pneumothorax

## Use Cases

- **Multi-label disease classification** (images can have multiple diseases)
- **Transfer learning** with ResNet, DenseNet, EfficientNet
- **Class imbalance research** (includes computed weights)
- **Medical imaging benchmarking** (reproducible splits)

## Compatibility

✅ TensorFlow/Keras `ImageDataGenerator`
✅ PyTorch `Dataset` and `DataLoader`
✅ scikit-learn pipelines
✅ Kaggle, Colab, Local environments

## Not Included

⚠️ **Images:** Use with base [NIH Chest X-Rays dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/nih-chest-xrays/data) (112K images, ~47 GB)
⚠️ **Expert labels:** This uses original NLP-extracted labels. For expert-validated labels, see NIH's separate release

## Citation

Wang et al., "ChestX-ray8: Hospital-scale Chest X-ray Database", IEEE CVPR 2017
